variable_description: The employer who reported the payment summary, as a key rather than as a number. Two rows for one payee in one year mean two payers, or one payer reporting under two ABNs, which is the usual shape for someone who changed jobs mid-year. The identifier is the only thing on the row that distinguishes employers, since nothing else describes the payer, and it is the same value for the same employer across the ATO products and DEX.
value_definition: A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as "a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register", structured as "a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded, cannot be checked against the public register, and is useful only for matching one record to another.
limitation: The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a workplace or a job. A large employer commonly holds several ABNs across its subsidiaries, so one job can look like several employers and a transfer within a group can look like a change of employer. An entity that restructures takes a new ABN, which breaks a continuous employment relationship in two. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed employer ABN on the payment summary tables. The Australian Business Register publishes the ABN's format, issuer and check-digit rule.
evidence_quote: The Australian Business Number (ABN) is a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register (ABR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Hashed employer ABN' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation.

variable_description: When the ATO took the extract this row came from, not anything about the taxpayer. Tax records keep changing after the income year closes, as returns are lodged late, amended and audited, so the same income year extracted at two dates is two different datasets. The suffix on the table name is that lag: ato_pay_sum_2223_12m is the 2022-23 year as it stood twelve months after the year ended. This column is what tells you which vintage you are reading, and comparing across years means comparing like lags rather than like income years.
limitation: The column describes the extract, not the person, so it is never an analysis variable. An early extract understates a year's income because late lodgers are missing, and the shortfall is not spread evenly: it falls on people with complex affairs and on those who lodge through an agent. Mixing lags across years builds a trend out of coverage rather than out of income.
rationale: The field is named as an extract reference on the ATO tables, and every product carrying it has a table-name suffix giving a lag in months from the end of the income year. ABS documents the administrative income sources as point-in-time extracts of tax records, but does not publish a definition of this column, so the reading is inferred from the naming and the table structure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'ATO data extract time' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left a reader with no reason to care about the column.

value_domain: ATO lump sum A type code
values: R: Paid out on termination for genuine redundancy, invalidity or an early retirement scheme
T: Paid out on termination for any other reason
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines: when an employee transfers or leaves
variable_description: Why the lump sum A on this payment summary was paid, which decides how it is taxed. Lump sum A is unused leave paid out when someone leaves a job, and the ATO splits it in two: code R covers unused annual leave, leave loading and post-1978 long service leave paid out for genuine redundancy, invalidity or an early retirement scheme, and code T covers the same kinds of leave paid out for any other reason. R is concessionally taxed and T is not, so the code is the difference between a redundancy and a resignation on an otherwise identical row.
value_definition: The ATO's lump sum type code, reported alongside the lump sum A amount. Only R and T apply to lump sum A; the other lump sum boxes on the payment summary carry their own separate amounts rather than sharing this code.
limitation: The code describes the reason the employer gave for the payment, not the circumstances of the departure. An employer that misclassifies a redundancy reports T, and nothing else on the row contradicts it. A row with no lump sum A amount carries no meaningful code.
rationale: The ATO's employer reporting guidelines set out the two lump sum type codes reported with lump sum A and what each covers.
evidence_quote: Lump sum type code R is for all unused annual leave or annual leave loading, and the component of long service leave that accrued from 16 August 1978 that is paid out on termination only for genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement scheme reasons.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Lump sum a type' with no domain and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the ATO publishes both codes.

value_source: Department of Home Affairs, visa list
variable_description: Which visa the traveller held on the movement record for the reference quarter. A subclass is Home Affairs' three-digit identifier for a specific visa product - 500 for a student visa, 482 for a skilled temporary worker, 189 for skilled independent - so it is the finest available statement of what somebody was entitled to do in Australia. Three of the values are not visas at all: the DIL records that Australian citizens are given 000, New Zealand citizens 444, and any other traveller with no valid subclass 001.
limitation: 000 and 001 are dump codes rather than visas, so filtering on a subclass silently drops citizens and anyone whose record failed to resolve. The subclass is taken from the reference movement, so it describes the visa held at that crossing and not the one held later; a person who changed status after arriving still carries their arrival subclass. Home Affairs publishes the subclasses but not the PLIDA code list, so the mapping between these values and the published subclasses is not confirmed.
rationale: The DIL states the derivation and names the three dump codes explicitly. Home Affairs publishes the visa subclasses themselves, but no published crosswalk to the values used here was found.
evidence_quote: australian citizens are allocated to the visa category 000 (dump code). new zealand citizens are to be allocated to the special visa category of 444.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's derivation text as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what a subclass is or warning that two of the values are not visas.

variable_description: The year the apprentice was born. limitation: With no day of birth, an age computed at any date is uncertain by up to a month either way. Combining this with DOB_M gives the finest available granularity; combining either with a date to get an exact age does not work.
rationale: The DIL's own text is a truncation of 'Year of birth'. ABS documents PLIDA as holding de-identified records with direct identifiers removed; no separate published definition of this field was found.
evidence_quote: Yof birth
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the mangled DIL text 'Yof birth' as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

variable_description: The month the apprentice was born, carried separately from the year because PLIDA holds no date of birth. Together with DOB_Y it gives age to within a month, which is the finest the asset allows. The month on its own is also the school-cohort variable: a January and a December birth in the same year start school a year apart, which shows up in age at apprenticeship commencement.
limitation: With no day of birth, an age computed at any date is uncertain by up to a month either way. The month alone is not an age and is meaningless without DOB_Y.
rationale: The DIL's own text is a truncation of 'Month of birth'. ABS documents PLIDA as holding de-identified records with direct identifiers removed; no separate published definition of this field was found.
evidence_quote: Mof birth
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the mangled DIL text 'Mof birth' as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

variable_description: The year the visa holder was born. PLIDA does not carry a date of birth: the day is removed and the year and month are supplied separately, so age can be computed to within a month and never exactly. Age at arrival is one of the strongest predictors of migrant outcomes, and this is the year half of the only age measure the asset offers.
limitation: With no day of birth, an age computed at any date is uncertain by up to a month either way. A year of birth reported on a visa application is as accurate as the identity document behind it, which for some humanitarian caseloads is an estimate.
rationale: The DIL's own text is a truncation of 'Year of birth' on the migrant demographics table. ABS documents PLIDA as holding de-identified records with direct identifiers removed.
evidence_quote: Yof birth
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the mangled DIL text 'Yof birth' as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Apprenticeships
variable_description: When an apprenticeship activity actually started. The journey table records a training contract as a sequence of activities - commencement, suspension, recommencement, cancellation, completion - and this is the start of one of them, not of the apprenticeship as a whole. Reading it as a commencement date counts every suspension and recommencement as a new apprenticeship.
limitation: The date is the actual date the activity started, which can differ from the date it was registered, so a file extracted soon after a period will be missing activities that started in it. The domain is inferred from the DIL wording; the department publishes the program but not this field.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as the actual date an activity started, on a table whose rows are the activities making up an apprentice's journey.
evidence_quote: The actual date an activity started.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without warning that an activity is not an apprenticeship.

value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Apprenticeships
variable_description: When an apprenticeship activity actually ended, or nothing if it was still running at the file's cut-off. The DIL states the cut-off explicitly, so a missing value is a right-censored activity rather than an error: the apprenticeship had not finished, not that the end date is unknown. Treating missing as unknown throws away every apprentice still training.
limitation: A missing end date means still running at the cut-off, so any duration computed from this column is censored and must be treated as such. The date is the actual end rather than the registered end, so recent periods are incomplete.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as the actual date an activity ended and states that a null means the activity was ongoing at the stated cut-off date.
evidence_quote: If null the activity was ongoing as of 31 December 2016
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the meaning of a missing value was buried in the description rather than stated as a limitation.

variable_description: When a service activity became available to deliver, not when anybody received it. The Data Exchange models a funded service as an activity with an availability window, and clients attach to it through separate session records, so this is a property of the funding arrangement. Using it as a service start date for a client attributes the whole activity's lifetime to everyone who touched it.
limitation: The date belongs to the activity, not to any client, and says nothing about when service was actually delivered. The domain is inferred from the DIL wording; the Data Exchange publishes its protocols but not this field's definition.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as the date a given activity is available for service, on the Data Exchange activity table rather than a client table.
evidence_quote: The date that a given activity is available for service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the date belongs to the activity rather than a client.

variable_description: When a service activity stopped being available to deliver, not when anybody stopped receiving it. Paired with STARTDATE it bounds the funding arrangement's life, so an activity ending is a program or contract closing rather than a client exiting.
limitation: The date belongs to the activity, not to any client. An empty value means the activity was still available at extract, so it is censored rather than unknown. The domain is inferred from the DIL wording.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as the date a given activity is no longer available for service, on the Data Exchange activity table rather than a client table.
evidence_quote: The date that a given activity is no longer available for service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.
